market_brief: Monday's Asia session split rather than extending Friday's rout: Kospi fell as much as 5.8% before paring to about -3%, while Taiwan's Taiex rebounded over 2% after its worst week since 1991 as Taipei widened short-selling curbs and said it is buying shares. US futures held their bounce (S&P +2.2%, Nasdaq 100 +3%, Nvidia pre-market about +6%) after Friday left the S&P at 6,910 (-3.7%, in correction), NDX -5.6%, SOX -10.7% and VIX 35.9. Havens are reversing too: gold rebounded about 2.4% to ~$3,620 after Friday's -4.6%, the dollar index eased to ~103.7 and bitcoin recovered to ~$61.5k. Rates stay central: CME pricing still shows ~92-93% odds of a December Fed hike despite Bessent's overtightening warning, with the 10Y at 4.91% (-24bp w/w); Brent near $90-92 is held up by reported tanker mine strikes in Hormuz. India opened modestly higher (Nifty ~25,827 at open) on record November FPI buying but trading has been choppy, with the rupee weakening and markets shut Tuesday.
ai_brief: The AI-capex scare is now the dominant lens: Morgan Stanley still sees hyperscaler capex up over 70% next year, while a report of Amazon nearing a ~$7.5bn deal for Decart and Ant-led funding for Simplexity show deal flow continuing. Releases were incremental — Thinking Machines' open-weight Inkling 2 Mini, Nvidia's Isaac robotics expansion and Google's Agent Compute Engine — and OpenAI floated a shared 'perplexity window' that labs would pause at until monitoring catches up. Supply-chain security remains a theme after Together AI disclosed a prompt leak caused by a coding agent committing a credential.

items.headline: Asia splits after the AI rout: Kospi slides as much as 5.8%, Taiwan rebounds over 2%
items.summary: South Korea's Kospi fell as much as 5.8% intraday and was down about 3.2% by 04:30 GMT, led by Samsung and SK Hynix, while the Taiex reversed early losses to gain about 2.5%. Hang Seng and CSI 300 pared losses to about -0.6%; Japan was shut for a holiday.

items.headline: US futures hold a 2-3% rebound; Nvidia indicated about 6% higher
items.summary: S&P 500 futures were up about 2.2% and Nasdaq 100 futures about 3% in Asian hours, with Nvidia up roughly 6% after falling 14% Friday and about 50% from its October level. The Goldman Sachs panic gauge reportedly sits at 9 of 10.

items.headline: Update: Taiwan says it is buying shares; Korea eases buyback limits as stabilisation steps widen
items.summary: New since Sunday: Taiwan widened short-sale curbs and said it is buying stocks, and South Korea is easing daily company-buyback limits for three months while preparing its stabilisation fund, last used in 2008. China eased minimum margin requirements.

items.headline: India opens higher on record FPI buying, then turns choppy as the rupee weakens
items.summary: Sensex opened about 228 points higher at 84,148 and Nifty at 25,827, helped by a reported record $13bn of November FPI buying and Rs 10,308 crore of inflows Friday. Live blogs later showed sharp swings, with Business Standard's headline citing a Sensex drop of about 900 points and the rupee past 93 per dollar.

items.headline: December Fed hike odds ease slightly to about 92-93% after Bessent's warning
items.summary: CME FedWatch-based reports put a 25bp December hike at roughly 92-93%, down from as high as 99%, with no pricing for 50bp; a further hike by January is priced at about 60%. Bessent said on CBS that financial conditions have tightened considerably and overtightening would be a mistake; the FOMC meets Dec 8-9.

items.headline: Gold rebounds about 2.4% to ~$3,620 after its worst week in eight months
items.summary: Spot gold climbed back above $3,600 in Asian trading as some of Friday's liquidity-driven selling reversed and the dollar index slipped about 0.2% to roughly 103.7. Copper held below $12,000 a tonne on the LME.

items.headline: Oil little changed as Hormuz mine reports offset equity-led selling
items.summary: Brent and WTI traded near flat after reports that two supertankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz and that Trump favours resuming military action against Iran after the new year absent a deal. HDFC Sky counts at least 22 reported attacks on shipping in November.

items.headline: Friday's damage by name: Nvidia -14%, Dell -11%, Anthropic -8.5% in its first full session
items.summary: Reuters data show Nvidia closed at $125.53 (-23% over five days), Dell -11% ahead of Tuesday's results and Morgan Stanley -5.3%, while newly listed Anthropic fell 8.5% to $88.91. Morgan Stanley still forecasts hyperscaler capex rising over 70% next year to above $1.6tn.

items.headline: Korea's early-November chip exports reportedly up 294% y/y despite the equity rout
items.summary: ANZ noted that South Korea's first-20-day November exports were strong, with semiconductor shipments up 294.4% from a year earlier, a contrast with the Kospi's slide to a 10-month low. Gartner projects global AI-related investment at $2.7tn in 2026.

items.headline: Dollar softens; yen near 159, PBoC fixes yuan at 6.7120
items.summary: The dollar index slipped about 0.2% with EUR/USD near 1.0996 and GBP/USD 1.3124, while USD/JPY hovered around 158.9-159 ahead of the December BoJ meeting. The PBoC set its USD/CNY midpoint at 6.7120; NZD reportedly sits near a 17-year low.

items.headline: European futures point modestly higher after the worst week in months
items.summary: Euro Stoxx 50 futures were up about 0.4-0.5% after the cash index fell 2.8% Friday; German 10Y yields are around 3.29%. Flash November PMIs and remarks from ECB's Lane and BoE's Pill are due today.

items.headline: WallStreetBets went quiet after the crash, then Nvidia mentions reportedly tripled
items.summary: A Medium analysis of Reddit chatter says WSB activity dipped for two days after the selloff before Nvidia mentions surged, a sign retail dip-buying interest is returning. Prediction-market traders have also been pricing odds on Jensen Huang's return, per Fortune.

items.headline: Bitcoin recovers to about $61.5k after briefly dipping below $56k over the weekend
items.summary: Bitcoin rose about 1.2% and ether about 0.8% in Asian hours, tracking the rebound in US equity futures. The weekend low below $56,000 was its weakest level since September 2024.

items.headline: Today: flash PMIs, Fed's Williams, ECB's Lane, HPE and Zoom; Dell Tuesday, PCE and GDP before Thanksgiving
items.summary: Monday brings global flash November PMIs, speeches by Fed's Williams, ECB's Lane and BoE's Pill, and HPE and Zoom earnings. Dell reports Tuesday, US PCE and GDP land mid-week before Thursday's Thanksgiving close, and Indian markets are shut Tuesday.

items.headline: Amazon reportedly nears a ~$7.5bn deal for AI startup Decart
items.summary: Amazon is reportedly close to acquiring Israeli AI startup Decart, valued around $4bn in May, with an announcement possible around AWS re:Invent from Nov 30. Neither company has confirmed.

items.headline: Thinking Machines releases open-weight Inkling 2 Mini for laptops
items.summary: The 26.4B-parameter mixture-of-experts model activates 3.4B parameters per token, needs about 20GB of memory and runs via Ollama on 32GB Macs. The company says it is weaker on multi-turn chat and constraint-heavy instructions.

items.headline: Nvidia expands Isaac with a reference humanoid and Isaac Lab 3.0
items.summary: Nvidia unveiled the Agile ONE SN reference humanoid (shipping early 2027), an open-source Isaac OS runtime, general availability of Isaac Lab 3.0 and a 2,000+ asset SimReady library.

items.headline: OpenAI proposes labs pause scaling at a shared 'perplexity window'
items.summary: Jakub Pachocki published internal pretraining log-perplexity figures and proposed frontier labs avoid crossing a 0.68-0.70 range until monitoring research catches up. It is a proposal, not a binding commitment.

items.headline: Google launches Agent Compute Engine to run agents in isolated VMs
items.summary: The managed service runs AI agents in small virtual machines with credentials kept outside the workspace and lets sessions resume from checkpoints.

items.headline: Together AI discloses prompt leak after a coding agent committed a credential
items.summary: Together said a coding agent pushed a credential to a public GitHub repo, exposing some customer prompt samples; review of possible personal-data exposure is ongoing. It follows OpenRouter dropping Together and two other providers.

items.headline: Ant Group leads $100m round for humanoid maker Simplexity at $1.6bn
items.summary: Hangzhou-based Simplexity Robotics raised a $100m pre-Series A with Alibaba, Tencent and HongShan participating. F-Prime separately projects 2026 robotics investment at $60.7bn, up from $22.1bn in 2025.

items.headline: Defense-AI startup Agon raises $70m Series A at $450m
items.summary: The round was led by former Sequoia chief Roelof Botha; Agon builds simulation models for autonomous drones, naval and ground robots.

items.headline: Apple starts Siri AI rollout in its apps with a limited developer preview
items.summary: New Siri AI features are shipping across eight Apple apps while third parties get a limited TestFlight preview of App Intents; the features are not available in the EU on iOS. Bloomberg's Gurman says recent Siri layoffs hit the legacy team, not the new AI group.

items.headline: US and China reportedly explore joint AI guardrails
items.summary: Semafor reports Washington and Beijing are exploring shared AI guardrails after Trump and Xi agreed that major military AI decisions should involve humans, per Bessent. Separately, UN talks on autonomous weapons ended without a binding ban.

items.headline: Trending repos: localcode for Apple Silicon agents, Worker755, Ai2's ACE2.5
items.summary: mjwsolo/localcode is an Apache-licensed CLI for local autonomous coding agents bundling 12 models; Worker755 is a Show HN browser game where an LLM treats the player as its subagent; Ai2 released the 46M-parameter ACE2.5-ERA5 climate model.
